sections.h2: Which Watauga County office handles my property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work. Tax Administration, in Suite 21 of the courthouse at 842 West King Street in Boone, appraises property and lists it. The Tax Collector's Office in the same suite is solely responsible for collecting taxes and fees. Office hours on the county page are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, except holidays.

The county lists 828-265-8021 for the listing department and 828-265-8036 for collections. Watauga County's mission statement for the tax office is to assess and collect taxes on all real and personal property in the county.

Watauga County sits in the Blue Ridge Mountains of northwestern North Carolina. It was formed in 1849, Boone is the county seat, and Blowing Rock, Beech Mountain and Seven Devils are the other incorporated towns in its tax rate table. A parcel's bill depends on which of those jurisdictions and which fire district it falls in.

sections.h2: What are the Watauga County property tax rates?
sections.html:
The county's tax rate page lists a rate for the county and one for each town, plus fire districts. The figures below are copied as printed under the 2026 column. The page does not print a unit beside them, and it does not say when the board set them, so ask the tax office to confirm the rate and unit that apply to your bill.

Watauga County tax rate page, 2026 column as printed
Tax districtPrinted figure
Watauga County (G01)0.318
Boone (C02)0.44
Blowing Rock (C03)0.44
Seven Devils (C04)0.47
Beech Mountain (C05)0.65
Boone Fire Service District (F02)0.06
Municipal service district (MS1)0.1575

Most fire districts print 0.05, with Stewart Simmons at 0.085 and Todd at 0.07. Other lines on the page include a Boone municipal motor vehicle fee of $30.00 and a solid waste user fee of 115.00 per year. Add the county figure to the figure for your town and your fire district, as the page lays out, to see the combined rate for a parcel.

sections.h2: When is Watauga County property tax due and when does interest start?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1 for the fiscal year they cover. Under G.S. 105-360, payment before January 6 is at face amount, and from January 6 interest begins at two percent, then three-fourths of one percent a month from February 1.

The Watauga collector adds its own rules. To avoid interest or penalties, a payment must reach the collector's office or be postmarked by the due date. Metered mail does not count as postmarked, and a metered envelope is treated as received on the day it is delivered.

Listing is a separate step. Listing forms go out the first week of January, and the regular listing period runs through the last working day of January. Property to be listed includes untagged motor vehicles, real estate improvements and business personal property, and applications for farm use or exempt status are due by January 31.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Watauga County tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay by mail, in person, online, by e-check, by card or by phone. Mail goes to the Watauga County Tax Collector, 842 West King Street, Ste. 21, Boone, NC 28607, with the account number and parcel ID on the check. A depository drop box sits at the front entrance of the courthouse.

  • E-check carries a $1.50 convenience fee.
  • Credit cards carry a 2.50 percent convenience fee with a $2.00 minimum, and the county does not receive it.
  • Consumer debit cards carry a flat $3.50 fee.
  • The phone payment line is 1-828-540-6193, with the same fees.

Sellers who close in the middle of the year usually have the closing attorney pay the bill from proceeds. The collector's page also says that the order of collection under G.S. 105-321(b) has the effect of a court judgment without court involvement, and enforced collection begins once bills are delinquent.

sections.h2: What happens if Watauga County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, with penalties and interest added, under G.S. 105-355. The county can foreclose on real property for delinquent taxes, which requires a court order and is handled by a law firm in Boone, according to the collector's page.

From March 1 to June 30, unpaid real estate accounts must be advertised, and the taxpayer pays an additional cost for that advertising.

An owner who has fallen behind can still sell. Back taxes, interest and costs are paid from proceeds at closing. Ask the Tax Collector's Office for a payoff figure in writing before the closing date.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Watauga County property assessment?
sections.html:
Appeal to the county board of equalization and review, which under G.S. 105-322 is made up of the county commissioners unless a separate board is created. Its first meeting falls no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May, and in a revaluation year it finishes by December 1.

Ask for a hearing in writing or in person before the board adjourns. If the board mailed notice of its decision fewer than 15 days before adjourning, you have 15 days after the mailing. The board mails its decision within 30 days after adjournment.

The next level is the state Property Tax Commission. Under G.S. 105-290, written notice of appeal with the grounds is due within 30 days after the board mailed its decision, with a copy to the assessor.

Counties must reappraise every eighth year as of January 1, per G.S. 105-286. Ask Tax Administration for the date of Watauga County's next reappraisal and its appeal schedule.

sections.h2: What property tax relief is available to Watauga County owners?
sections.html:
North Carolina has three relief programs for permanent residences, and an owner can receive only one. The elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value, under G.S. 105-277.1. The owner must be 65 or totally and permanently disabled and under the income limit, which NCDOR prints as $38,800 for 2026.

The disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 of appraised value and has no age or income limit. The circuit breaker limits tax to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent above the limit up to 150 percent of it, with a $58,200 upper figure for 2026.

Apply on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, not the state. The county tax listing page points seniors age 65 and older to that form. State rules say it should be filed during the listing period and must be accepted through June 1.

sections.h2: How does the tax bill affect selling a Watauga County house?
sections.html:
The bill follows the property, so any unpaid amount is settled at closing. Circuit breaker owners should know that deferred taxes for the preceding three years come due on a transfer. Check the parcel's jurisdiction first, since a Boone address pays differently from a rural parcel in a fire district.

If you need a quick sale with taxes owed, you can request a cash offer on this site, and the payoff gets taken from the price at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Watauga County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Tax Collector's Office, Suite 21 of the courthouse at 842 West King Street in Boone. A drop box is at the courthouse front entrance.

faqs.q: Does the Watauga County Tax Collector count metered mail as postmarked?
faqs.a: No. Metered mail is not considered postmarked, so it is treated as received when it is delivered to the collector's office.

faqs.q: When are Watauga County listing forms mailed?
faqs.a: The first week of January, with the regular listing period running through the last working day of January.

faqs.q: What fee applies if I pay Watauga County taxes by credit card?
faqs.a: The county prints a 2.50 percent convenience fee with a $2.00 minimum on credit cards, and a flat $3.50 on consumer debit cards. The county does not receive the fee.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal to the Property Tax Commission?
faqs.a: Thirty days after the county board mailed its decision, by written notice stating the grounds, with a copy to the county assessor.
